region_scheme.name: oregon-bbox-elev-v1
region_scheme.description: Ordered first-match rules over longitude, latitude and DEM elevation, with the Cascade crest as a latitude-dependent line anchored on the volcanoes. Oregon's south border is the 42nd parallel exactly; its north and east borders are piecewise-linear approximations of the Columbia and Snake rivers, accurate to about 0.05 deg -- half a cell of the 0.1 deg weather grid, where it was an eighth of a cell of the 0.4 deg grid used before 2026-10-17 -- and to about one cell in the short north-south reach of the Columbia below Longview. Points with no classified land cover (ocean, outside NLCD) are excluded by the caller before assignment.
region_scheme.elevation_source: renderer DEM elevation grid (USGS), sampled at the weather grid point
region_scheme.land_mask: NLCD classified-land validity; points with no classified land (ocean, outside NLCD) are dropped before assignment
region_scheme.aggregation: unweighted mean over the region's weather grid points; each point contributes one value per day, and the 0.4 deg cells differ in area by under 8% across the state

statewide.name: Oregon (statewide)
statewide.definition: every summarised grid point inside the state on classified land; the state spans a rainforest and a desert, so this is a lede, not a forecast

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Coast & coastal valleys
regions.definition: lon <= -123.6 and elevation < 1000 ft: the beach plain from Astoria to Brookings AND the coastal river valleys behind it (Nehalem, Siletz, Alsea, Smith), which share its marine climate. Ocean points are excluded by land cover, not by this rule

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Coast Range
regions.definition: lat >= 43.4, lon <= -123.1 and elevation >= 1000 ft: the timbered ridge between the coast and the Willamette Valley. The eastern limit is -123.1 because the Coast Range does not reach further east at any latitude; a looser limit put the Umpqua National Forest in it

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Siskiyous & southwest interior
regions.definition: lat < 43.4 and west of the tapering Klamath-Siskiyou eastern edge (-122.35 at the California line, -123.2 by lat 43.4): the Siskiyou and Klamath mountains with the Rogue and Umpqua valleys they enclose

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Willamette Valley
regions.definition: lat >= 43.4, -123.6 <= lon <= -122.0 and elevation < 1000 ft: the valley floor, farmland and metro included, and at this grid spacing the continuous lower-Columbia lowland north of Portland with it

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Cascade crest
regions.definition: within 0.35 deg longitude of the crest line (interpolated between Hood, Jefferson, the Sisters, Diamond Peak, Crater Lake and McLoughlin) and elevation >= 4000 ft

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: West Cascades
regions.definition: anything west of the crest line not already claimed above: the wet western slope and its foothills. Deliberately unbounded below in elevation, so that the west side is covered exhaustively and no western point can fall through to a rule meant for the east

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Columbia Basin
regions.definition: lat >= 45.0, lon >= -121.4 and elevation < 3500 ft: the dry northern lowlands, from the Deschutes mouth east along the Columbia and Umatilla and on into the lower Grande Ronde and Snake canyons

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: East Cascades
regions.definition: from the crest line to 1.4 deg of longitude east of it: the dry eastern slope and the Deschutes and Klamath plateaus below it. Bounded on BOTH sides -- an eastern-slope rule with no western bound silently collects every western point the rules above missed

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: Blue Mountains
regions.definition: lat >= 44.2, lon >= -119.5 and elevation >= 3500 ft: the Blue, Wallowa, Elkhorn and Strawberry ranges

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider

regions.name: High Desert
regions.definition: everything else in the state: the Basin and Range and Owyhee country of the south-east

soil_temp_f.extremes_basis: daily MEAN (the series carries no sub-daily soil extremes), so the real swing is wider
